resources.string: Connect with the API PIN of your TTO heating controller.
Connect your phone to the Wi-Fi network of the controller itself.
Go to SETUP → API PIN and copy the PIN shown there.
Switch back to your normal Wi-Fi and enter the PIN below.
No controller found for this PIN.
Get the PIN from the controller
Be on your home Wi-Fi or on the controller’s own Wi-Fi.
Find your controller and pick it by name.
Enter its 4-digit dashboard PIN. OnlyHeat reads the API PIN and signs you in.
The heating server is not responding. Try again.
%1$s follows its schedule, so the controller kept %2$s. Turn the schedule off on the controller to set it manually.
The controller did not accept the change and kept %1$s.
Uses your target temperature and the AccuWeather forecast, with a ±2° margin, to balance comfort and economy.
This does not work on the controller’s current firmware (the AccuWeather forecast is unavailable before 1.0.9.2.0). Turn it off, or update the controller.
The controller did not accept the change.
The controller did not accept the change (this room follows its schedule).
Saved on this device since %1$s, fills in over time
Not enough history saved yet. It builds up on this device from now on; the 24 h tab shows the last day.
While an entry is active, the room holds its temperature and ignores manual and smart settings.
The schedule can only be edited while your phone is on the Wi-Fi of the controller, or on the home Wi-Fi the controller is connected to.
Cannot reach the controller. Check your Wi-Fi connection and try again.
No schedule entries. Rooms use the temperatures set in the app.
The 4-digit PIN you use to log in at http://192.168.42.1/dashboard.
The controller's Setup page shows no API PIN.
OnlyHeat needs local network access to reach the controller.
The controller will reboot. Heating control and its Wi-Fi will be unavailable for a minute or two.
If your phone switches to another Wi-Fi meanwhile, connect it back to the controller.
The app could not confirm that the controller came back. Check its connection and try diagnostics again.
Set when each room holds a fixed temperature.
Use this when the controller stops responding, instead of switching it off at the breaker.
Schedule and restart work only while your phone is on the Wi-Fi of the controller, or on the home Wi-Fi the controller is connected to.
Signed in to the TTO cloud with your API PIN.
Run this when the app cannot reach your heating.
The controller is online. You only need to be on its Wi-Fi or your home Wi-Fi for the schedule and restarting.
The controller is running, but its connection to the cloud is down. Restarting it should fix this.
The app could not reach the controller through the cloud or the local addresses it checked. Connect to the controller’s own Wi-Fi and check again.
Tap “Unverified dashboard” and choose your controller by name.
Join the controller’s network in Wi-Fi settings, then tap Retry. If prompted about no internet, stay connected.
Its firmware changed from %1$s to %2$s. If the schedule, restart or finding the controller stop working, update OnlyHeat.
Choose your controller by its Wi-Fi name.
No named controllers found. Try the controller’s own Wi-Fi.
More than one controller reports %1$s. Connect to its own Wi-Fi to tell them apart.
Your phone cannot reach the TTO cloud. Check its internet connection.
Rooms are at %1$s°. Their own temperatures are saved.
Away is on, but these follow their schedule and kept their temperature: %1$s
2° warmer for a while, then back to the current target.
Notifies you when the controller goes offline, a room gets too cold or a window seems open. Checks about every 15 minutes.
The cloud lost contact with your heating controller. Open OnlyHeat → Controller → Connection check.
Your heating controller is back online.
%1$s dropped %2$s° since the last check. Is a window open?
